# PhotoFrame

<!-- Generated by Auto (Composer) - 2026-05-21 -->

Full-screen photo slideshow for old browsers (including Safari on iPad 1). Java backend + plain HTML/ES5 frontend.

## Features

- Display one photo at a time, full screen or sized with **width**, **height**, and **position** in pixels (editable on `/myphotoframe.html`; photo fits inside the box, aspect ratio preserved)
- **Timer** advances to the next image (interval in seconds, URL parameter)
- **Click or tap** the image to show the next photo immediately
- Image source: **local folder** on disk or **Google Photos** (picker selection)

## Requirements

- **Java 11** or newer (JDK 11+)
- Maven 3.6+

## Dependencies

HEIC → JPEG uses [Openize HEIC](https://github.com/openize-com/openize-heic-java) (pure Java). The library is resolved from the Aspose Maven repository (see `pom.xml`); no macOS `sips` or system tools required.

## Run

```bash
cd photoframe/backend
mvn spring-boot:run
```

Open: **http://localhost:8082/** (query parameters on `/` are preserved; you can also use `/index.html?...`)

Put JPEG/PNG/GIF/HEIC files in `photoframe/images/`. HEIC files are converted to JPEG when served (pure Java via Openize HEIC), so older browsers can display iPhone photos.

## Deploy (tar.gz package)

Build a ready-to-install archive (JAR, scripts, templates, data folders):

```bash
./scripts/build-deploy-tar.sh
```

Output: `dist/photoframe-deploy-1.0.0.tar.gz`

On Linux (Java 11+). The package `run.sh` uses **`/volume1/java/current/bin/java`** by default (edit `java.env` if needed):

```bash
tar xzf photoframe-deploy-1.0.0.tar.gz -C /volume1/photoframe
cd /volume1/photoframe/photoframe
cp google-photos-credentials.properties.template google-photos-credentials.properties
# edit google-photos-credentials.properties
./run.sh
```

See `README-DEPLOY.txt` inside the archive.

## Deploy (JAR only)

```bash
./scripts/package.sh
java -jar backend/target/photoframe.jar
```

Run from the **photoframe** project directory so `./google-photos-credentials.properties` and other paths resolve. Or set `PHOTOFRAME_*` environment variables (see `application.properties`).

## Slideshow layout (`/myphotoframe.html`)

On **myphotoframe.html**, use **Slideshow display** to set width, height, position (X, Y) in **pixels**, and **interval** (seconds between photos). The image is scaled to fit inside that rectangle without cropping. Use **0** for width or height to fill the full window on that axis. Values are saved to `slideshow-display.json`. The slideshow reloads settings on each photo and every 15 seconds.

## URL parameters (slideshow only)

Layout and timer interval are **not** set from the URL (except optional `interval` override) — use **myphotoframe.html** or `slideshow-display.json`.

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| `interval` | from saved settings | Optional URL override of seconds between photos |
| `folder` | from config | Local folder path override (only when `photoframe.source=local`) |

Examples:

```
http://localhost:8082/?interval=15
http://localhost:8082/?interval=60&folder=./images
```

## Configuration (`backend/src/main/resources/application.properties`)

| Property | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `photoframe.source` | `local` or `google` (not overridable from the slideshow URL) |
| `photoframe.local.folder` | Folder for local images (default `./images`) |
| `photoframe.timer.seconds.default` | Default interval if URL omits `interval` |
| `photoframe.google.credentials.path` | Path to Google OAuth properties file |
| `photoframe.google.picked.file` | JSON file for picker selection (default `./google-photos-picked.json`) |

## Google Photos setup

1. Enable **Google Photos Picker API** in Google Cloud Console.
2. Create OAuth **Web** client (Playground redirect URI); obtain refresh token with scope:
   `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/photospicker.mediaitems.readonly`
3. Copy `google-photos-credentials.properties.template` to `photoframe/google-photos-credentials.properties`.
4. Set `google.photos.client.id`, `client.secret`, and `refresh.token`.
5. Set `photoframe.source=google` in `application.properties`.

**Important:** You cannot list your whole Google Photos library in the slideshow. Use the **Picker** to choose which existing photos to show ([API updates](https://developers.google.com/photos/support/updates)).

### Choose photos

Open **http://localhost:8082/myphotoframe.html** (or `/myphotoframe`; `/pick` and `/pick.html` still work):

1. Click **Add photos from Google Photos** (opens Google’s picker in a separate window).
2. Select photos from your library (search by date, filename, etc.).
3. When done, PhotoFrame appends new picks to `google-photos-picked.json` and the slideshow uses it.

Google’s picker **cannot** pre-check photos you already chose on PhotoFrame; remove unwanted photos on `/myphotoframe`.

Re-open `/myphotoframe` to add more photos, remove individual photos, or clear all.

The slideshow shows clear errors when something is wrong (0 images, auth), with a link to the pick page.

Images are proxied through the server (`/api/photos/serve/{id}`) so the browser does not need Google auth headers.

## API

| Endpoint | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `GET /api/photos/next?format=text` | Next image URL (plain text for legacy browsers) |
| `GET /api/photos/next` | JSON `{ success, id, url, mimeType }` |
| `GET /api/photos/serve/{id}` | Image bytes |
| `GET /api/photos/config` | Default source and timer |
| `GET /api/photos/google/status` | Picked photo count and list |
| `GET /api/photos/google/picked` | Full selection with thumbnail URLs |
| `DELETE /api/photos/google/picked/{id}` | Remove one photo from selection |
| `DELETE /api/photos/google/picked` | Clear entire selection |
| `POST /api/photos/google/picker/session` | Start Google Photos picker |
| `GET /api/photos/google/picker/session/{id}` | Poll until user finished picking |
| `POST /api/photos/google/picker/session/{id}/import` | Merge new picks into selection |

## Structure

```
photoframe/
  backend/     Spring Boot (port 8082)
  frontend/    index.html (ES5 slideshow), myphotoframe.html
  images/      Local photos folder
```
